Minutes slipping.means: His minutes have dropped in recent games compared with his season average.
Minutes slipping.why: Prop lines are built from season averages, so shrinking minutes can quietly cap how much a player can produce; recent games are the better guide.
Minutes slipping.example: Nov 9: Dejounte Murray played 18 minutes (usually 34) in a 51-point blowout.

Blowout risk.means: The game is expected to be lopsided (a big point spread).
Blowout risk.why: When a game is decided early, starters often sit the fourth quarter, so counting stats can fall short of their averages.
Blowout risk.example: Oct 26: Derrick White played 18 minutes (usually 34) as BOS beat CHI 134-99.

Teammates push the other way.means: Key teammates are out, which can raise or lower a player's role compared with normal.
Teammates push the other way.why: When a high-usage teammate sits, shots, minutes and assists move to others, so the usual average may not apply tonight.
Teammates push the other way.example: Oct 28: with Luka Doncic out, Austin Reaves' usual workload shifted, so his average was a weak guide.

Line already moved.means: The number has changed since it first opened.
Line already moved.why: A move means new information has already been priced in (injury news, matchup, volume), so some of the edge may be gone.
Line already moved.example: Oct 27: a Jayson Tatum points line opened at 26.5 and moved to 25.5.

Tough matchup.means: The opponent ranks among the best at defending this player's position.
Tough matchup.why: Strong positional defence can lower efficiency and volume compared with the player's season numbers.

Early season.means: The player has only a handful of games this season.
Early season.why: Small samples swing a lot; one big or bad night can distort an average, so treat averages as shaky.
Early season.example: Early November: several rotation players had only 3 or 4 games of data.

Role change.means: His role has shifted (starter vs bench, usage up or down).
Role change.why: Older games may not describe tonight, so weight recent role over the season average.
Role change.example: A starter moved to the bench loses minutes even if he plays well.

Projection disagrees.means: The model's projected stat sits on a different side of the line than the lean suggests.
Projection disagrees.why: When data and the lean point opposite ways, confidence should be lower.
Projection disagrees.example: A model projecting 13.5 against a 12.5 line while the lean pointed under.

Injury tag.means: The player or a key teammate carries an injury designation.
Injury tag.why: Status can change close to tip-off, which changes minutes and roles; always re-check before the game.
Injury tag.example: A starter ruled out an hour before tip shifts everyone's role.
